title: Frequently asked questions
subtitle: Short guide for administrators, staff, and field teams — aligned with the current WinProx Facility app.

how_it_works.title: How does WinProx work?
how_it_works.intro: WinProx follows one core flow: issue → tasks → completion. Time (punch clock) is optional; ESG (measurements) is also optional.
how_it_works.summary: Sites and units, issues via QR or admin, approval on the public portal, tasks per team, follow-up via dashboard, briefing, and calendar. Time (punch clock) optional; ESG optional.

steps.title: Sites and units
steps.text: Create locations and add units (machines, zones, or areas), one by one or in bulk. Under Places, Categories, Locations and Units are separate. Link a team to a unit so tasks land automatically.

steps.title: Create an issue
steps.text: Administrators and staff report in the app (with up to 4 photos). Reporters scan the unit QR and do the same in the browser — no app installation required.

steps.title: Approval (public)
steps.text: New issues via QR are blurred on the public portal until an administrator or staff member approves them. In admin, you always see everything in full.

steps.title: Tasks for teams
steps.text: An issue can have multiple tasks, each assigned to one team. Also schedule recurring maintenance via the calendar.

steps.title: Field work via QR
steps.text: Field workers sign in via the Clock Point QR (name + icon) and complete tasks via the unit QR — without a WinProx login.
steps.highlight: Clock Point = sign in (name + icon); clocking in requires Time (punch clock); unit QR = tasks and issues on site.

steps.title: Follow up and close
steps.text: Track progress in the dashboard, briefing, and calendar. Complete tasks with notes and photos; close the issue when work is done.

how_it_works.box_body: Under People → Teams create at least one team — in a small organisation Hotel or Facility is enough. Link the team to categories. Via Clock Point and unit QR, workers record updates and photos on site.

pricing.title: How much does WinProx cost?
pricing.intro: You start with a free trial month (50 units, including Time punch clock). IoT, ESG and API are not in the trial. Then choose 10, 50 or 100 units per year. Time (punch clock) is optional afterwards. Corporate is custom (more than 100 units or when API/webhooks are required).
pricing.summary: Trial up to 50 units, including Time (punch clock). IoT, ESG and API on Corporate. Then 10/50/100 per year.
pricing.content_note: Unit = object or place with a QR. Document = file on the QR portal, maximum 1 per unit. Photos on issues are unlimited. Exact prices are under Subscription.

qr_code.title: Which QR codes are there?
qr_code.body: Unit QR: reporters submit issues; workers (after Clock Point sign-in) handle open tasks on that unit and can — when category and unit both allow unit checks — record OK/Not OK. Clock Point QR: workers sign in (name + icon) and see their team tasks; clock in/out only with Time (punch clock). Location QR: general link to the site. Everything opens in the browser — no app.
qr_code.summary: Unit QR (reports/tasks/unit check), Clock Point QR (sign-in; clocking with Time), location QR — all in the browser.

reporter_portal.title: How does the reporter portal work?
reporter_portal.intro: Scanning the unit QR opens a web page for that unit. Reporters describe problems; approved issues and shared documents/announcements are visible. Workers with team access can complete open tasks and — when enabled — run unit checks.
reporter_portal.summary: Unit QR portal: report, approved issues, documents, announcements, on-site tasks and optional unit check for workers.

sections.title: New issue
sections.text: Describe the problem and optionally add up to 4 photos. Photos are resized on the device before upload. First name, last name and email are optional unless the administrator required contact details (category and unit). Signed-in workers do not need those fields. Anti-spam limits apply (e.g. at most one report every few minutes per device).

sections.title: Awaiting review
sections.text: Until an administrator or staff member approves, text and photos remain blurred on the public portal. In admin, everything is readable immediately.

sections.title: Open issues
sections.text: Overview of approved, active issues for this unit, with status.

sections.title: Documents and announcements
sections.text: Shared manuals and announcements for the site or unit, with language choice and automatic translation when available.

sections.title: Tasks on site
sections.text: Field workers signed in via Clock Point and belonging to the team start and complete tasks via the unit QR.

sections.title: Unit check (workers)
sections.text: Workers only, after Clock Point sign-in, and only when the administrator enabled unit checks on category and unit. Record OK or Not OK, optionally with a checklist. OK does not create an issue; after Not OK a normal report can follow.

moderation.title: Why is content on the QR portal blurred?
moderation.body: Public QR pages blur description and photos until an administrator or staff member approves the issue. This prevents inappropriate or incorrect content from being publicly visible. Admin screens (dashboard, issues, tasks) always show everything in full — that is where you review content.
moderation.summary: Blur only on public QR portals until approval; admin never blurred.

photos.title: How do photos work for issues and tasks?
photos.body: When reporting an issue or completing a task, you can add up to 4 photos. On phone and in the browser, they are compressed first (faster upload). In admin, photos are shown clearly; on the public portal they remain blurred until the issue is approved.
photos.summary: Up to 4 photos, client-side compression; blur only on public portal before approval.

time_clock.title: What is the Time module / Clock Point?
time_clock.body: Time is the optional punch clock: field workers clock in and out via the Clock Point QR (breaks and shifts included). Clock Point remains the sign-in QR (name + icon) even without Time. Time is included in the trial. On a paid WinProx plan it is optional; you add it on Subscription.
time_clock.summary: Time (punch clock): clock in/out via Clock Point. Optional, not included by default.

esg.title: What is ESG & Compliance?
esg.body: ESG is an optional module on WinProx Corporate to record measurement values during recurring inspections (energy, safety, …). Administrators see indicators, measurements and follow-up tasks. Link an indicator to a recurring issue; measurements via portal or API.
esg.summary: ESG module on Corporate: indicators, measurements and follow-up for recurring inspections.

for_who.title: Who is WinProx for?
for_who.body: For facility organisations — factories, care, municipalities, campuses — that want issues, internal teams, field follow-up, optional Time (punch clock) and optionally ESG or IoT Connect in one place. No separate hospitality or contractor portals: one Facility app.
for_who.summary: Facility organisations: issues, teams, field work; Time (punch clock) optional; ESG and IoT on Corporate.

user_roles.title: How do the different users work?
user_roles.summary: Administrator: full control and subscription. Staff member: daily follow-up. Field worker: field work via Clock Point and QR without login.

roles.title: Administrator
roles.text: Full control: sites, issues, tasks, team, subscription, colleague accounts, and (where applicable) API settings.

roles.title: Staff member
roles.text: Daily follow-up of sites, issues, and tasks. No management of subscription or colleague accounts.

roles.title: Field worker
roles.text: Works without a WinProx login. Signs in via Clock Point QR; starts/completes tasks via the unit QR, with photos and notes.

data_export.title: Can I export my data?
data_export.body: Yes. Go to Settings → Privacy & data export. There an administrator can download a machine-readable export (JSON in a ZIP) of the account and relevant activity in your environment. Keep the file safe.
data_export.summary: Administrators export via Settings → Privacy & data export (GDPR).

delete_account.title: How do I delete my account / organisation data?
delete_account.body: Only an administrator can do this. Go to Subscription → Delete organisation data. First download an export via Settings → Privacy & data export, then confirm with password and email. During a trial you can permanently delete yourself afterwards. On a paid plan there is a 7-day wait; WinProx administration performs the deletion. You can cancel until then via Subscription. Media files (photos, documents) are not kept in the recovery snapshot. If the trial ends without a subscription, WinProx sends warnings and may delete the organisation automatically (default around day 14 after trial end).
delete_account.summary: Admin: Subscription → delete data (export + password + email; trial self-serve, paid via WinProx after 7 days; expired trial may auto-delete).

internal_teams.title: How do I set up internal teams?
internal_teams.body: Start small: one team (for example Hotel or Facility) and everyone who carries out tasks in it. Go to People → Teams. A team leader is not required. Extra teams only if there are genuinely separate groups. Link teams to categories. Add workers manually, or via CSV/Excel. Under Teams you also manage unit-check checklists. Print the Clock Point QR for the floor (Time → Clock Points).
internal_teams.summary: One team is enough to start. People → Teams; link to categories; Clock Point QR.

team_follow_up.title: How do teams follow up on tasks?
team_follow_up.body: Tasks appear in Tasks, on the calendar, in the briefing, on the Clock Point QR and on the unit QR. Workers start and complete on site. Coordinators follow status in admin. Recurring issues generate cycles with planned due dates; recurring tasks show the Recurring pill.
team_follow_up.summary: Follow-up via Tasks, calendar, briefing and QR; recurring cycles with Recurring pill.

reservations.title: How do reservations work?
reservations.body: Reservations are for shared resources with a time slot (meeting rooms, vehicles, keys) — not for defect reports. Turn on Reservable on the category and Allow reservations on the unit (off by default). Guests book via the unit QR (30 min hold + email confirmation). Staff create, edit and cancel bookings; overlapping slots are blocked.
reservations.summary: In the app: Reservations menu (and calendar). Category Reservable + unit Allow reservations (off by default); guest books via QR with email confirmation.

multiple_locations.title: Can I manage multiple sites?
multiple_locations.body: Yes. Under Places you manage Categories, Locations and Units separately. Multiple locations and units in one organisation, with filters. Limits depend on your subscription.
multiple_locations.summary: Multiple locations and units via Places (Categories, Locations, Units); limits per plan.

page_help.title: Where do I find help on a screen?
page_help.body: On most screens, a ? appears next to the title. It opens page help with actions and — where relevant — explanations of statuses (new, in progress, done, closed). On public QR portals, the same help appears in the header.
page_help.summary: Use the ? button next to the page title for action and status help.

mobile.title: Does WinProx work on a smartphone?
mobile.body: Yes. Admin is desktop-first but usable on tablet. Field and QR portals are mobile-first. Field workers work on their phone via Clock Point and unit QR. Dark theme is handy on phone.
mobile.summary: Browser on phone/tablet/desktop; field via QR is mobile-first.

install.title: Do I need to install software?
install.body: No. WinProx is a web app. Coordinators and field teams work in the browser, with no separate installation or app store.
install.summary: No installation — everything via the browser.

dynamic_qr_codes.title: Dynamic QR codes
dynamic_qr_codes.body: Dynamic QR stickers can later be linked to a different unit. Print in bulk (e.g. Avery sheets), stick on site, scan while signed in, and assign a unit. Static codes stay fixed to one unit.
dynamic_qr_codes.summary: Dynamic QRs re-linkable; print bulk stickers and assign a unit on site.

stickers.title: Which stickers can I use?
stickers.body: For printing we recommend Avery or Herma labels (A4). In Sites, download a sticker sheet (Word) in the correct format. Optionally set a sticker background or organisation logo under Settings.
stickers.summary: Avery/Herma A4; sticker sheet from Sites; optional logo/background in Settings.

style.title: WinProx style and Custom portal style
style.body: Under Settings, choose WinProx style: Standard or Dark (for the app). Custom portal style is optional: background and button colours (and optional background photo) for the public QR portal that reporters and field workers see.
style.summary: Standard/Dark for the app; optional custom colours/background for the QR portal.

api_webhooks.title: API and webhooks?
api_webhooks.body: On Corporate (or when API is enabled) manage API tokens and outgoing webhooks (HMAC-signed) under Settings. Connect WinProx to other systems for issues, tasks, unit checks (unit.check.recorded), ESG measurements and more. IoT Connect uses a separate gateway token for sensor ingest (Corporate).
api_webhooks.summary: API tokens and webhooks under Settings (Corporate); issues, tasks, unit checks, ESG; HMAC deliveries. IoT ingest via gateway token (Corporate).

iot.title: What is IoT Connect?
iot.body: IoT Connect links sensor gateways to WinProx (Corporate). Alarms (e.g. water leak, door open too long) automatically create an approved issue and task. Sensor readings can also be stored as ESG measurements. Manage gateways, sensors and rules under IoT Connect; the gateway sends events to POST /api/v1/iot/events with a gateway token.
iot.summary: IoT Connect on Corporate: sensor alarms → issues; readings → ESG. Gateway token ingest.

unit_checks.title: What are unit checks?
unit_checks.body: Unit checks are quick OK/Not OK confirmations on the unit QR by field workers (after Clock Point). Enable first on category and unit (off by default). Optional checklists are managed under Teams (shared or linked to a team; starters for cleaning, technical and security) and linked per unit. For OK all points must be ticked. History and filters in Unit checks; webhook unit.check.recorded for integrations. Separate from issues and ESG measurements.
unit_checks.summary: OK/Not OK via unit QR (enable category + unit); checklists under Teams; OK does not create an issue; webhook unit.check.recorded.
